title: An Open Day at Our School
description: Review of music and arts, food and drink, and a school visit; like / (not) as ... as, some / a lot of / lots of, at / in / on.
content:
Last Sunday, our school held an Open Day for new students and their parents. It started at 9 a.m. in the school yard.

In the morning, visitors visited the school facilities, such as the library, the computer rooms and the art room. In the art room, they saw paintings by gifted students. Some of the paintings looked like photos. The visitors also watched a concert in the hall. The school band played classical music, which is not as loud as rock music, so the parents enjoyed it.

At noon, everyone had lunch in the canteen. There was a lot of delicious food: spring rolls, fried chicken and fresh fruit. Some students cooked pancakes, and the visitors ate lots of them.

In the afternoon, the visitors went home. A little girl said to me, "I want to study at this school next year." I felt very proud.

options.A: A school's Open Day, with art, music and food for visitors

questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 describes art and music, paragraph 3 describes food, and paragraph 4 describes the end of the Open Day.
The paintings by gifted students looked like photos, suggesting that these students are very talented.

questions.explanation: The school band played classical music. A band is a group of musicians who play together.
The writer felt proud after hearing that a little girl wanted to study at the school. Proud means feeling pleased about something good.

options.B: It was successful and the visitors enjoyed it.

questions.explanation: The parents enjoyed the music, visitors ate lots of food, and a girl wanted to study at the school. These details suggest that the Open Day was successful and enjoyable.

questions.question_text: What can we infer about the little girl?

options.A: She did not like the school.
options.B: She was already a student there.
options.C: She liked the school and wants to join it.
options.D: She was afraid of the teachers.

questions.explanation: False. The school band played classical music, not rock music.

questions.question_text: The visitors had lunch in the school garden.
questions.explanation: False. Paragraph 3 says everyone had lunch in the canteen, not in the school garden.

questions.question_text: The visitors bought some books at the Open Day.
questions.explanation: Not Given. The passage mentions a library but does not say that visitors bought any books.
